about.title: Cupertino Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Cupertino households rely on everything from kitchen appliances to imported electronics to campus-area vehicles, and when one of those products fails, the injuries can be sudden and serious. Unlike many personal injury cases, California product liability claims often rest on strict liability: if a product left the manufacturer with a defect in its design, its assembly, or its warning labels, and that defect caused harm, the injured person generally doesn't have to prove anyone was careless. That said, these cases move fast — the defective item itself is often the most important piece of evidence, and it can get lost, repaired, or discarded before anyone realizes its importance. If a product hurt you or someone in your family here in Cupertino, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these claims and can advise on next steps, including how to preserve the product.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: California often allows product liability claims to proceed under strict liability, meaning the focus is on the defect and the harm it caused rather than proving someone was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product, giving an attorney more avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: Because the product itself is often central to these cases, an attorney can advise you early on how to keep it safe and intact for review.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law often applies strict liability, so the focus is generally on whether the product was defective and caused your injury, not on proving negligence. An attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without repairing or discarding it. The product is frequently the most important piece of evidence in these claims. An independent attorney can advise you on safe storage and next steps.

items.question: Is this only about products bought locally in Cupertino?
items.answer: No — products purchased anywhere, including through Cupertino-area retailers or delivered to homes near De Anza Boulevard or Stevens Creek Boulevard, may be involved in a claim. What matters is where the defect caused harm, not just where it was purchased.
